messages:
maria (Recruiter): Heads-up 1: internal conversion: contractor Remy P wants to convert to FTE. Current contractor rate $90/hr. Hiring team proposes base $170,000 + no sign-on. This is above L2 band top ($145k). Candidate prefers conversion date 2026-06-01 to keep benefits continuity. Need comp exception for above-band and guidance on any make-whole payment for guaranteed contractor earnings.

sam (People Ops): Important: when converting contractors we avoid retroactive "make-whole" payments that could imply employee misclassification. If we need to bridge retention risk, comp committee typically approves a one-time conversion bonus (taxed as income) instead of backdating salary. Routing to comp committee required.

tia (Hiring Manager): Remy has been on 30+ hrs/week for 6 months and has competing offers. If we don't match market, they'll take an external role mid-May. Manager asks for base $170k to reflect L2+ seniority and requests approval for a $12k one-time conversion bonus to offset transition. Can we get decision within 72 hours? Candidate start contingent on notice period.

kevin (Finance): We need to see total run-rate impact. Two levers: raise base to $170k (ongoing) or keep base at band and approve $12k one-time. From budget POV, one-time is cheaper for FY26 but will still appear in headcount forecast. Also payroll notes: conversion bonus processed on first payroll run after start; need to confirm proration rules.

elaine (Legal): Confirming sam's note: avoid any payment structure that could be seen as retroactive contractor wages for periods already invoiced. Document contractor dates and prior SOWs. A conversion bonus is standard and legally safe if documented as a sign-on/conversion incentive. Include IP/invention assignment check as part of conversion packet.

hr-bot: Automated: Comp exception CE-2026-089 opened. Required attachments: recruiter packet, manager justification, contractor engagement records, proposed FTE offer. SLA: 72 business hours due to internal conversion policy.

maria (Recruiter): Offer draft uploaded (drive.redwood/internal/remy_p_offer.pdf). Note: candidate needs benefits enrollment effective first pay period after 6/1. Also they requested equity acceleration (partial vest) for contractor time 1: this is unusual; do we allow credit for prior contractor service when calculating vesting?

sam (People Ops): Equity credit for contractor time is uncommon; comp committee must approve any retroactive vesting. Alternatives: larger one-time RSU grant or a short cliff-shift on new grant. I'll flag this to comp chair.

olivia (Comp Chair): Reviewing CE-2026-089 now. Given retention risk and accurate documentation, my preferred route is: approve base at band cap ($145k) + $12k conversion bonus + a one-time RSU grant (value ~ $10k) to compensate for prior service. This keeps ongoing comp predictable while addressing candidate expectations. Will confirm by EOD.

tia (Hiring Manager): :thumbsup: to Olivia's proposal if it keeps Remy. Please confirm how quickly payroll can execute the conversion bonus so candidate gets assurance.

kevin (Finance): Payroll can deliver one-time payment within 2 pay cycles after start date. If we need same-day commitment letter, we can include language "conversion bonus payable after start and subject to standard taxes and withholding."

maria (Recruiter): I'll share Olivia's provisional offer language with Remy and request 24 hour feedback. Thanks all for quick turnaround.

olivia (Comp Chair): Final: CE-2026-089 approved per option: base = band top $145,000; conversion bonus $12,000 (one-time); one-time RSU grant $10,000 notched to IC2 entry grant schedule. Conditions: contractor records attached, legal sign-off on SOW closure, payroll proration confirmed. Closing note: no retroactive salary backpay.

hr-bot: Automated: CE-2026-089 status updated: APPROVED. Please attach final offer and confirm start date in ticket.

maria (Recruiter): Offer accepted verbally by Remy. Candidate requested 2026-05-25 start; manager requests 2026-06-01 to align benefits. I'll set 6/1 and note pay/prorate details. Closing thread.
